# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._  Precious metal prices were generally weak in the final days of March with only gold managing to hold onto any gains in Dollar terms despite a relatively firm Euro. The initial downwards impetus came from concerns over European debt and slowing Chinese growth, sending all of the metals to lows on the 22nd of March. A strengthening Euro provided support and each metal moved higher, with further impetus provided by comments from Ben Bernanke on the 26th that US accommodative policies were likely to be maintained. The strength was temporary, though, with the complex sagging lower since that point. In the first weeks of 2012, the more industrial metals had outperformed gold but now the tables were turned: gold regained its recent premium over platinum to suggest that risk appetite had decreased noticeably.  After the previous week’s long liquidation of futures positions, investors treated the precious metals complex with a little more discrimination leading up to the 27th of March. Gold positioning rebounded, climbing by two million ounces. However, futures investors continued to be bearish on the more industrial precious metals, with short positioning rising and long positions being closed for palladium, platinum and silver.  ETF flows in the last week of March were more positive than in the preceding week. Gold saw a little net selling but nothing like the 500,000 ounces sold a week earlier. Platinum and silver saw buyers tempted in by lower prices and recorded net inflows of metal into their funds. Palladium too saw buying interest but this was outweighed by heavy selling from one of the smaller funds. **David Jollie david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **02 April 2012** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **02 April 2012** ### **Gold CFTC data to 27 March 2012; ETF data to 30 March 2012.** **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

Unsurprisingly, fears over European debt and a Chinese economic slowdown hurt the more industrial metals more than gold. Nevertheless, gold’s price performance was not exciting, suggesting that investor attention has moved elsewhere for the moment. What was perhaps more interesting as a gauge of market sentiment was that gold moved back over platinum, suggesting that a global economic recovery is by no means a certainty. During the week, gold did fall as low as $1,630 on the 22nd before rallying to $1,695 on the 27th following assistance from a weak Dollar and comments from Ben Bernanke suggesting that “accommodative policies” might be maintained. The boost was short-lived though, with selling reemerging to leave gold at $1,670 at the end of the month. -  Net long speculative COMEX positions bounced by 2.2 million ounces in the week to the 27th of March, with short-covering of some futures positions accompanied by addition to outright long positions. The response of futures investors to the decline in price has been rather lukewarm, with positions now some 7.7 million ounces lower than at the end of February. There are two possible interpretations of this move: a los of investor confidence or space for a move higher at some point. We feel that a sense of short term bearishness has entered the market and that the reality lies between these two positions. -  After the previous week’s net ETF selling of almost half a million ounces of gold, the final week of March was more neutral with only 16,000 ounces sold. Worryingly, however, the majority of funds which we monitor recorded net outflows of metal (roughly balanced by buying in GLD/ SPDR). As we wrote last week, this suggests that investors are beginning to become a little less convinced of the bullish case for gold. Total positions now stand at 70.4 million ounces. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Mar12** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

-  The last ten days of March were relatively quiet for the silver price which traded only in a $2 range. The initial move during this period was lower as the after-effects of the 29th of February sell-off continued to erode investor confidence. Silver continued to drift lower from nearly $37 then to a low of $31.15 on the 22nd as gold fell. At this point, a stronger Euro provided some assistance, helping silver back to a high of $33.16 on the 27th before confidence waned once again, with silver falling back to end the month close to $32.50 per ounce. Currently, silver is largely following the gold price and showing little independence but it may be ch

allenging for silver to maintain this performance if futures investors continue to liquidate their positions. -  In the silver market, net long speculative positions decreased for a fourth successive week, dropping by 15.7 million ounces to 169.1 million ounces on COMEX. Since the end of February, positioning has fallen from 257 million ounces. Little additional short interest has been seen but long positions have been pared back to more reasonable levels. Although the silver price fell back sharply at the end of February and the start of March, it has been surprisingly robust, finding support above $32 despite this reduction in futures interest. -  After two weeks of net selling, silver ETF positions increased by 910,000 ounces to 460 million ounces in the final week of March. The buying interest was fairly widespread with a number of funds recording fresh buying interest. Overall, though, there is still no clear indication of momentum amongst ETF silver investors. 3 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **02 April 2012** ### **Platinum CFTC data to 27 March 2012; ETF data to 30 March 2012.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Platinum Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**||||**TOCOM**|**Net total**|**Price**| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| |||_Futures_

-  Platinum trading was mixed in the final days of March. Initially, the price fell from the 21st over concerns of slow or slowing Chinese economic growth. Interestingly, platinum underperformed gold even as gold struggled with platinum moving back into an unaccustomed discount to the yellow meta

l. Overall, platinum declined from $1,680 on the 19th to a brief low of $1,605 on the 22nd before the selling dissipated. A firmer Euro helped provide a little support for platinum and the other metals and investors did the rest of the work in taking the price back up to $1,665 on the 27th. Bearish sentiment slowly descended on the market though and, with gold weak, platinum softened towards support at the $1,640 level. -  Net long speculative NYMEX positions in platinum dropped for the fourth successive week. Investors shed a further 112,000 ounces as positions slid from 1.78 million ounces at the end of February to 1.61 million ounces at the end of March, as TOCOM positions climbed by 36,000 ounces. The selling has been quite orderly and mainly driven by long liquidation. However, a recent rise in the number of open short contracts could indicate further price weakness ahead. -  Platinum bulls breathed a sigh of relief in the final week of March as ETF investors returned tentatively to buying mode after three successive weeks of selling had been seen. While there was a small amount of selling of metal from one of the smaller funds, this was outweighed by some gentle buying in the European ETFS fund. Total holdings currently stand at 1.49 million ounces, thirty thousand ounces below their March peak. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **02 April 2012** ### **Palladium CFTC data to 27 March 2012; ETF data to 30 March 2012.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Palladium Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**

-  In the second half of March, palladium emphatically fell below support at $700 per ounce to touch a low of $641. Of itself, this price decline was not too surprising. Of greater concern was the fact that no real attempt was made to recapture this level. On the 22nd, disappointing Chinese PMI data set a bearish tone and all of the precious metals were sold. Having been flirting with the $700 level a day earlier, palladium dropped to a low of $650 on the 22nd before finding support. The Euro strengthened slowly but steadily against the US Dollar, providing some respite and helping palladium recover a little of its lost ground in reaching $670 on the 27th. Gentle selling pressure re-emerged to send palladium to close to $640 on the 29th although it has since recovered to $659. -  Having slipped below $700, palladium lost some of its appeal to investors who cut their net long exposure to palladium in response. In the week to the 27th of March, NYMEX positioning fell by 291,000 ounces, their largest weekly fall since September 2011. Net positioning remains moderate by historical standards at 911,000 ounces following a spell of long liquidation and additions to short positioning. Non-commercial short positions climbed to 3,200 contracts but this remains much lower than in Q4 last year. -  While platinum saw net ETF buying in the final week of March, palladium saw a mixture of buying and selling even as the price failed to rebound following its fall from $700. US investors proved to be positive, buying half a tonne of metal, treating the price fall as a buying opportunity. However, there was a large sale of metal from one of the smaller funds we monitor, which drove net positions down by 8,000 ounces in the week to 1.97 million ounces. We believe that this is likely to have been the action of a single investor and feel that the dominant view is that current prices provide a buying opportunity. 5 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** #### **Disclaimer:** This briefing is for our clients’ information purpose only.
